findings.rationale: From round 11 WA's feature distribution jumps by about 1.2 federation SDs (largest shift on HighBP, with GenHlth and AgeGroup also moving), and this persists through round 20. The same round-11 break shows in its updates: cosine with the median update falls from about 0.99 (round 8) to 0.26 at round 11 and turns negative (-0.59 by round 19), while the norm ratio jumps. Local AUC (0.80) and prevalence look normal, and the drift shows in the feature statistics, so this is a data drift rather than poisoning. Its size-adjusted norm ratio is not flagged.

NE's features shift by about 1 federation SD from round 11 onward (AgeGroup, then HighBP and GenHlth), and the shift is sustained through round 20. Over the same window its update cosine drops from about 1.0 (round 6) to 0.26 at round 11 and then turns negative (-0.68 by round 20), with the norm ratio rising from about 1.2 to 2.4. Local AUC is 0.78 and the prevalence is normal, pointing to a data change rather than label noise or poisoning.

UT shows a feature shift of about 0.8 to 1.1 federation SDs from round 11 onward, mainly on GenHlth and HighBP, and the largest shift overall (1.17 SD) comes from the same round-11 break. Its update direction is also anomalous: its mean cosine is 0.34 with a minimum of -0.57, and its update norm is high. Local AUC (0.80) and prevalence look normal, which fits drift rather than label noise.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex and AgeGroup), then confirmed suspicions with per-round drift and update queries on NE, UT, WA and GU. Three clients (NE, UT, WA) show a consistent break at round 11: feature distributions shift by roughly one federation SD (GenHlth, HighBP, AgeGroup), update cosine with the median falls from about 1 to negative, and update norms rise, while local AUC and prevalence stay normal. I report these as drift with onset round 11. Other flags were not reported: GU (small n=708, CITL z=-3.8 and norm-ratio z=+3.8, below the threshold and not corroborated), the AgeGroup subgroup outliers (GA, CT, WY, CA; z_noise at most 4.3, and all in the over-prediction direction, not under-diagnosis), and the sex and age subgroup outcomes overall. Budget is fully spent (0.0 left).
